rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Columbia was the Apollo 11 command module, part of the command and service module. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

That command and service module was built by North American Aviation. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Answer: North American Aviation.

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters of Oxygen tank No. 2 ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours before launch. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in that tank. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

I did not cite the thermostatic-switch cause as a fact line, because the opened notes state it only in a description, not in a fact line.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not say how or when he died, or which seat he won.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was Oxygen tank No. 2. Its shelf description says it is an "Apollo 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion" ([[oxygen-tank-2]] description: "Apollo [unverified] 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion"). The service module carried the oxygen tanks: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The Apollo 11 crew member who piloted that kind of spacecraft was Michael Collins, the command module pilot: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The notes do not describe any other part he played in the landing.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?

The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. The crew built it from radioed instructions. The adapter was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round. rows.question: List every Apollo mission in the brain that launched with a crew, with its launch date.
rows.answer:
Four Apollo missions in the brain launched with a crew:

- **Apollo 8**: [[apollo-8]] "[stated] Launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 11**: [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Launched 1969-07-16 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Its crew was Armstrong, Aldrin and Collins, per its links to [[neil-armstrong]], [[buzz-aldrin]] and [[michael-collins]].
- **Apollo 13**: [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Its crew was Lovell, Haise and Swigert, per its links to [[jim-lovell]], [[fred-haise]] and [[jack-swigert]].
- **Apollo 16**: [[apollo-16]] "[stated] Launched 1972-04-16 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". Its crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke, per its fact "[stated] Crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

Apollo 1 is not included. Its crew died in a cabin fire during a launch rehearsal, so it never launched. [[apollo-1]] "[stated] A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
The earlier citations dropped the `[stated]` tag that starts each fact line. Here they are again with the full line, minus only the leading `- `.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. The mission goal also changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew splashed down, having used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

Later in 1970, the review board report was published in June. This is an investigation date, not a mission event. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

citations.quote: [stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)
[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)
